recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Sum the coefficients
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the whole question. The coefficients are 1, 4, 9, … — the squares — so their sum is the standard result n(n+1)(2n+1)/6.
steps.memory_tip: The coefficients 1, 4, 9 are the SQUARES, so their sum is n(n+1)(2n+1)/6.

recall.must_convey: That the coefficients are the squares 1², 2², …, n², whose sum is n(n+1)(2n+1)/6.
accept: the coefficients are the squares so their sum is n into n plus one into two n plus one over six
recognise one four nine as the squares and use the sum of squares formula
add the coefficients using sigma n squared
coefficients squares kabatti sum of squares formula vaadali
the sum is n n plus one two n plus one by six

steps.why: The whole bracket is one angle, and its coefficient is what the period formula needs. Recognising 1, 4, 9 as squares is what makes that coefficient findable.
common_mistakes: Treating each term as a separate function with its own period.
Using the sum of n rather than the sum of n².

steps.label: Apply the tangent formula
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Dividing π by a fraction with 6 underneath brings the 6 up top, which is where the 6π comes from.
steps.memory_tip: Period of tan kx is π/|k|, and dividing by a sixth brings the 6 up top.
lines: Period of tan kx = π/|k|, with k = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6

recall.must_convey: That the tangent period formula gives 6π/[n(n+1)(2n+1)].
accept: pi divided by that fraction gives six pi over n into n plus one into two n plus one
the six comes up top so the answer is six pi over the product
the period is six pi by n n plus one two n plus one
six pi by n into n plus one into two n plus one
dividing brings the six to the numerator
heard_as: n n plus one two n plus one

steps.why: Dividing by a sixth multiplies by six, which is why a 6 appears in a formula that started with none.
